nm2_1_modeling_methods.detail: CentileBrain used to generate regional volumetric z-scores; specific normative modeling algorithm not specified in this paper.
nm2_1_modeling_methods.supporting_text: Individual regional volumetric z-scores were generated using CentileBrain (Ge et al., 2024), an open source online software tool that leverages an aggregated neuroimaging dataset with a large number of individuals (37,407 comparison brains).

nm2_2_response_variable.detail: Regional subcortical gray matter volumes of 7 bilateral structures: amygdala, caudate, hippocampus, pallidum, putamen, thalamus, and accumbens area. Volumes were obtained using FreeSurfer (version 6.0) as part of the HCP Minimal Preprocessing Pipeline.
nm2_2_response_variable.supporting_text: Measurements were obtained for regional subcortical gray matter volumes of the bilateral amygdala, caudate, hippocampus, pallidum, putamen, thalamus, and accumbens area (Fig. 1a). These 7 regions were chosen based on prior literature showing selective impacts from PAE.
nm2_2_response_variable.location: Gimbel2025.pdf.md: Section 2.4. MRI acquisition and processing

nm2_3_explanatory_variables.detail: The CentileBrain tool calculates z-scores adjusted for age, sex, and total intracranial volume (ICV). ICV includes white matter, gray matter, cerebrospinal fluid, vasculature, blood, and other tissue. Right and left subcortical regions were examined separately.
nm2_3_explanatory_variables.supporting_text: These scores represent the degree of each participant's regional volumetric (dis)similarity to typically-developing individuals of the same age and sex, adjusted for total intracranial volume (ICV). As a result of extensive modeling of possible covariates completed during development of the tool, CentileBrain uses ICV, which includes white matter, gray matter, cerebrospinal fluid, vasculature, blood, and other tissue (Ge et al. 2024).
nm2_3_explanatory_variables.location: Gimbel2025.pdf.md: Section 2.5. Derivation of norm-adjusted volumetric scores
